Assets/Kolkata/MOSS TTS Nano/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md
============================================================

# Third-party notices

MOSS-TTS-Nano is by OpenMOSS. Upstream: https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano

This modified C# implementation ports the fixed ONNX sampling, voice-clone prompt construction, and streaming codec state handling from `ort_cpu_runtime.py` and `onnx_tts_runtime.py` at commit `cc7bdf19c7639c0870dab22045a33b442760f6be`, the version used by this repository's voice-cloning benchmark. It adds Unity lifecycle handling, bounded PCM delivery, shared transcript tags, and provider switching. The upstream Apache-2.0 license is included in `LICENSE`.

Models copied from the benchmark's local cache:

- OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M-ONNX, reviewed revision `f52645cb467506d8e18e746ddd59482685b74e58`.
- OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano-ONNX, reviewed revision `ceff0d0749bfb3fa2d61149794ec6feef0d1e1ae`.

Model licenses and notices accompany the StreamingAssets bundle. The runtime also uses the project's existing ONNX Runtime, SentencePiece, and Pocket TTS audio utilities; their existing licenses continue to apply.

Re-audited against main `8b7bcc9` on 2026-09-16: the two upstream runtime files are unchanged from the original pinned commit, and both model repository revisions above remain current. See `UPSTREAM-AUDIT.md` for the additional local audio/memory corrections.

# MOSS-TTS-Nano model bundle

OpenMOSS models, Apache-2.0. License included in `LICENSE`.

- https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M-ONNX
- https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano-ONNX
- https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano

Copied from the existing `Python/VoiceCloning` ONNX benchmark cache. Upstream filenames and external weight-file layout are preserved. See `model-files.sha256` for the included files' hashes and `Assets/Kolkata/MOSS TTS Nano/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` for implementation provenance.

Why Three Licenses?
===================

The zlib License could have been used instead of the Modified (3-clause) BSD
License, and since the IJG License effectively subsumes the distribution
conditions of the zlib License, this would have effectively placed
libjpeg-turbo binary distributions under the IJG License.  However, the IJG
License specifically refers to the Independent JPEG Group and does not extend
attribution and endorsement protections to other entities.  Thus, it was
desirable to choose a license that granted us the same protections for new code
that were granted to the IJG for code derived from their software.

============================================================
ThirdParty/MsvcRuntime/README.md
============================================================

# App-local Microsoft C++ runtime

The Windows ONNX Runtime package imports `MSVCP140_1.dll` in addition to the base
MSVCP/VCRUNTIME libraries. The RX 570 crash report loads the Windows System32 ONNX
stub (version 1.0.1911.2111), which lacks `OrtGetApiBase`; it lists the base C++
runtime DLLs but no MSVCP140_1. A missing dependency is a likely reason Unity fell
back to that incompatible system DLL, although the player log cannot prove which
dependency lookup failed.

`Windows-x64` contains the complete x64 CRT redistributable family from the
installed Visual Studio 2026 Community `VC/Redist/MSVC/14.51.36231` directory.
The Windows build processor validates the recorded SHA-256 hashes and copies
the matched family beside the player executable. It does not change the system
installation. Early player initialization loads the game's ONNX library by
absolute path and reports the Win32 error if loading fails.

These Microsoft binaries are redistributed under the Visual Studio license,
not the project's source license. Source and version are recorded in
Windows-x64/manifest.json. Microsoft deployment guidance and redistribution list:

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/deployment-in-visual-cpp
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/releases/2026/redistribution

Keep the family together when updating; do not copy arbitrary System32 versions.

Whisper's `ggml-cpu.dll` also imports `VCOMP140.DLL` (Microsoft OpenMP). Include
`vcomp140.dll` from the same version's `x64/Microsoft.VC145.OpenMP` directory;
the CRT directory alone does not supply it. Its hash and additional source are
recorded in the manifest, so the existing build processor validates and copies
it beside the executable along with the CRT files.

The September 26 report `Player (23) (1).log` reports an unavailable dependency
of `libwhisper.dll` and repeated recognition failures while Pocket TTS continues
generating audio. The missing OpenMP redistributable is a verified packaging gap,
but that log does not identify the exact dependency that failed on the player's
machine. The other report, `Player (24) c++ error.log`, does not contain this
loader failure or a native fault stack; the runtime popup still needs an
affected-machine reproduction. Whisper also imports `vulkan-1.dll` through
`ggml-vulkan.dll`, even when CPU recognition is selected.

ThirdParty/WhisperCompatibility/README.md
============================================================

# Windows Whisper compatibility

The three supplied launch logs contain two machines: Radeon RX 550 (PCI device
699F) and RX 570 (67DF). Both crash inside `ggml-vulkan` while Whisper initializes;
the RX 550 stack also contains Bandicam/OBS Vulkan hooks. These logs do not show
TTS exhausting memory.

`Windows-x64/ggml.dll` rebuilds **only the backend registry** from whisper.cpp
v1.7.5, matching the pinned whisper.unity package. Its exported ABI is checked
against the original DLL. CPU kernels, Vulkan kernels, libwhisper, weights, and
inference settings are unchanged. The two changes skip Vulkan registration and
dynamic Vulkan discovery when `KOLKATA_WHISPER_CPU_ONLY=1`. `use_gpu=false` alone
does not bypass this version's Vulkan registration; hiding devices also happens
after Vulkan instance creation, too late for these crashes.

WindowsSpeechCompatibility sets the variable before scene initialization for
AMD device IDs 699F and 67DF, or the explicit Steam launch option `-whisper-cpu`.
Other devices retain GPU recognition. The variable can also be supplied by a
launcher. This is a compatibility workaround, not a claim that every card with
these IDs crashes; recognition may be slower on those CPUs.

The Windows build processor replaces the player's registry only after checking
all shipped Whisper DLL hashes against `build-manifest.json`. A package update
fails the build until the compatibility library is reviewed/rebuilt. Editor and
non-Windows native packages are unchanged. Do not edit Library/PackageCache.

Rebuild with `python Tools/WhisperCompatibility/build.py` (Visual Studio C++, x64).
The script downloads a hash-pinned upstream archive and retains its MIT license.
Run `python Tools/WhisperCompatibility/verify.py` for isolated CPU/GPU recognition
and ONNX loading checks. It uses the existing English model and voice fixture,
performs three recognition turns per backend, and saves logs under Temp.

Upstream: https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/tree/v1.7.5

Shipping validation still needs a player run on the affected hardware. The
microphone/C++ report ends normally and has no native fault stack; the CPU launch
option allows a controlled comparison without guessing at a TTS fix.
